---
title: "Reporting risk and withholding cost"
subtitle: "2.4 · after Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), slides 23–25"
description: "Expected wrong directions and withholding costs in the posterior risk of a grade report."
---

A wrong stated direction costs $1$ and withholding a pair costs $\tau$. Posterior risk $R_\tau = E/M + \tau(M-N)/M$ averages expected mistakes and withheld comparisons across all $M$ pairs.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **τ .20, at most 3 grades.** The best of 603 reports states 12 of 15 pairs (risk .0417); 2 (A and B; E and F) below-τ pairs stay withheld because the grade cap links pairwise decisions.
- **τ .20, no cap.** The best of 4,683 reports states 14 of 15 pairs (risk .0372), withholding only C–D.
- **τ .40, no cap.** The strict order states 15 of 15 pairs (risk .0480, entirely expected mistakes).
- **τ .30, no cap.** The optimal report is unchanged while its risk becomes .0438; open **Score your report** to evaluate any fixed grade vector beside it.

<details>
<summary>Model assumptions and source notes</summary>

We use the normal posteriors for score A at six fictional sites from the postrank tutorial. For these posteriors and the costs on the slider, the uncapped optimum states the pairs whose error is below $\tau$. Posterior risk is an expected cost per pair; the chance that at least one direction is wrong is a separate joint probability (postrank theory book, chapters 10–11).

</details>

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
library(postrank)
g <- c(A=1L,B=1L,C=2L,D=2L,E=3L,F=3L)
postrank_evaluate(g, pr_tutorial$one, weights=c(score_A=1), tau=.2)$primary_risk
```
This scores the displayed capped report directly. The package's solver-based tutorial also reports a floating-point correction to the lower bound; direct fixed-report evaluation needs no solver.
:::

Standalone: [open the app](../../embed/price-of-silence.html), for example `?tau=.2&cap=3&stage=2`.
